  • Cognitive load and worked examples
  • Explicit instruction
  • Feedback
  • Metacognition and self-regulation
  • Mastery learning
  • Collaborative learning
  • Reciprocal teaching
  • Formative assessment

B Promising

  • Interleaving
  • Elaboration
  • Concrete examples
  • Dual coding and multimedia principles
  • Flipped classroom
  • Growth mindset
  • Productive failure
  • Dialogic teaching
  • Universal Design for Learning
  • Generative learning

C Framework

  • Prior knowledge and advance organisers
  • Bloom's taxonomy
  • SOLO and constructive alignment
  • Backward design
  • Gradual release of responsibility
  • Rosenshine's principles of instruction

  • Motivation theories

D Theory

  • Behaviorism
  • Cognitivism
  • Constructivism
  • Sociocultural theory
  • Progressivism
  • Critical pedagogy
  • Humanistic perspective

E School model

  • Montessori
  • Waldorf (Steiner) education
  • Reggio Emilia
  • Freinet

F Contested or myth

  • Learning styles (VAK)
  • Multiple intelligences as a teaching method
  • Brain and working-memory training

Strong Meta-analyses of classroom studies show that teaching this way improves learning. Promising Controlled studies show gains, but results are mixed, small in number or dependent on context. Framework A useful structure for planning, with no intervention studies behind it as a method. Theory A way of explaining how learning happens. It shapes values and choices, but cannot be tested as a single intervention. School model A whole-school movement with its own philosophy and practice. Contested The research does not support using it as a teaching method, even though many teachers believe in it.

Ask any AI tool

Describe the problem, your subject and grade, and the approaches you are considering, strongest evidence first. Then ask for the reply in this format:

Reply in plain text, no tables, in exactly this format: BEST FIRST STEP: which approach to try first and why, given what the teacher sees NEXT LESSON: what it looks like in one concrete lesson in this subject, with minutes WATCH FOR: how the teacher will know within two weeks whether it is working AI: one way AI could help the teacher with this, and one way students' use of AI could make the problem worse HONEST NOTE: what the evidence label means for this approach, in one or two lines
